Per protocol_canonical_projection_pattern.md at meta-level. The
LIST walker $emit_let_locals had its OWN tag-arm dispatch (LBlock,
LIf, LMatch) parallel to the SINGLE walker $emit_let_locals_walk's
much fuller dispatch. Drift 7 (parallel-arrays) at the walk-coverage
layer: TWO sources of truth for "what containers descend."

Symptom: fn $query and fn $teach in src/pipeline.mn use `~>`
(LHandleWith) at top-body level. The fn body is `[LHandleWith]`.
The LIST walker's dispatch had no LHandleWith arm; recursion stopped
at the LowExpr; nested LLets (`let ast = ...; let q = ...; let
result = ...`) never declared in preamble. wat2wasm: 24 undef-locals.

Substrate fix: list walker handles LLet (its leaf-action — declare
the local) and dispatches ALL OTHER tags to single walker via
$emit_let_locals_walk. The single walker is the canonical source
of truth for container coverage; the list walker just declares at
its iteration position and delegates everything else. One walk-
coverage definition; consistency flows automatically.

  Post:   3 errors / 0 undef-locals / 1 undef-global / 2 redef-param

    Hβ.first-light.handler-closure-install per walk_handle.wat:386.

The seed at this point compiles the wheel CORRECTLY where the wheel

perennials/a83048e:
The model was a still life at mature size in an even light. Three things the
sheet cannot do now live in it, each on numbers the guide already holds or
that only she can give.

The years axis. Growth rate is in the record as three words, so the figure
grows along a band between a cautious and a generous reading of its pace,
today drawn solid with mature behind it as a dashed ghost, and a plant whose
pace the sources never recorded stands at mature size with the gap said out
loud rather than guessed. lib/growth.ts owns the band; the coverage line
counts how many figures actually have a pace.

The sun, from two numbers that are hers and rounded before they are kept: her
latitude to the whole degree (a degree is 111km, too coarse to place a house
and plenty for the sky) and her estimate of the sheet's span in metres. With
both, the ground stands at true scale and lib/sun.ts casts the real solar
position as a shadow across it, and each drawn bed reports about how many
hours of direct sun it gets, in the catalogue's own light words, and how many
of her kept plants are recorded for that light. She can save a bed as a spot.
Without both numbers nothing is cast and nothing is guessed; the offer stays
open. The bed shade is defined by the recorded crowns, uniformly, so the
shadow she sees is the shade the numbers mean.

Her decade as the dataset that does not exist. Where she has photographed a
plant the guide has none for, her photo stands up in its place at the recorded
height, with an invisible archetype mass casting the shadow so the shade still
matches the crown. A photograph of her plant beats any archetype of its kind,
and there is no open per-species model set that could do better.

And walk-in: the camera drops to eye level at the sheet's edge, for the day
the yard exists only on paper. All of it stays in the lazy three.js chunk.
perennials/a82694f:
Enrichment for plants already swept never re-checked, so coverage GloBI ingested
later would never be picked up and a failed lookup stayed failed forever.

A quarterly full re-sweep is the wrong fix. USDA flower color is static, GloBI's
coarse groups barely move for a plant that already has data, and 26,000 calls in
one afternoon four times a year is the rudest possible shape to aim at a small
academic service.

Re-verify the five stalest plants every hour instead. That cycles all 8,800 in
about ten weeks, costs seconds, heals failed lookups on its own schedule, and
picks up new coverage as it appears.

Two traps worth naming. rechecked_at has to survive a source refresh, or the
truncate would make the whole dataset look never-checked and it would re-sweep
itself every week. And the stamp is written even when a lookup fails, or a
permanently broken plant would stay "stalest" forever and wedge the rotation on
itself.
noodles/a80d83b:
Entries hold up to seven tones (a full 13th) and an inv field that
picks the bass from the first four - third inversion is as far as
the notation goes. harmonyChord names stacks by their ceiling (a 9
CONTAINS the 7th: five tones say 9, six say 11, seven say 13; the
7th's quality picks maj9 vs 9 vs m9) and spells slash basses in the
chord's own letters (C/E, G7/B). The bloom becomes the ladder: six
pads - 7 9 11 13 sus4 sus2 - each the whole diatonic stack up to
its number, named by the model so Gm11 and Cmaj9 read back as
themselves. Voicing is one shared shape everywhere (playback,
preview, the circle): the triad voice-leads for continuity, the
stack climbs tone over tone above it, and the sub voices the
inversion's bass - which is what an inversion IS to the ear. Pad
polyphony 4 -> 8 so a 13th and the previous chord's tail coexist;
idle voices stay silent subtrees.

Also measured, not cut: the DSP surgery ceiling. Bypassing all
three input comps AND the chorus on a dense wet render buys ~9%
(.tmp/dbg-dsp-cost.mjs) - the bill is the sound itself, so the
builder's crackle is not fixable by thinning and the suspects are
the tight-buffer toggle, battery-saver throttling, and stale-build
main-thread stalls. Editor inversion chips and the staff letter
gutter land next.

stoop/a84322f:
The app explained itself on every drawer: a hundred and ninety words on
the desk before the first button, two hundred and fifty on the scene, a
manifesto sentence at the top of each. Most of it is gone to the README
where it belongs; what stays is a line where a line is needed, in the
voice the toasts already had. A punk tool does not lecture, and a chill
one does not need you to understand it before you can use it.

A fresh press was seeded as a couples' newsletter: THE WEEK, REFLECTIONS,
LOOKING AHEAD, a sample journal entry about Sunday coffee and quiet. It
is blank now. The cover carries the zine's name and a nudge drawn by the
press rather than stored in the page, so it never reaches paper and never
has to be deleted; the other seven pages are empty; the sample scraps are
gone. Two sample pieces remain in the tray so the desk has something to
show, and they are meant to be cut.

The roster starts as one person, me, until somebody is added, and the
desk goes round whoever is actually there rather than alternating between
a and b: alone it is always yours, at two it alternates as before, at
four it comes back every fourth issue. The name is edited in the bar
where it is shown, and lands on the cover the moment you leave the field.
Handing an issue on sweeps the copier's lamp across the pages once, half
a second of CSS, because it is the one moment in the loop that should
feel like a machine did something.

Three assertions leaned on the sample content and now assert the blank
start instead. One of them also found that adding a person re-renders
the roster and drops an unsaved rename, which is the order a person
would do it in; the test saves first.
